bmt-2016-analysis-02.prompt:
Find an integer pair of solutions $(x,y)$ to the following system of equations.
$$\log_2(y^x)=16,\qquad \log_2(x^y)=8.$$

bmt-2016-analysis-03.prompt: A half-mile long train is traveling at a speed of $90$ miles per hour. As it enters a $1$ mile long tunnel, Steve starts running from the back of the train to the front of the train at a speed of $10$ miles per hour. When Steve is out of the tunnel, he stops running. How far along the train has Steve run in miles?

bmt-2016-analysis-04.prompt: A geometric progression starting at $a_0=3$ has an even number of terms. Suppose the difference between the sum of the odd-indexed terms and the sum of the even-indexed terms is $39321$ and that the sum of the first and last term is $49155$. Find the common ratio of this geometric progression.

bmt-2016-analysis-07.prompt:
Find the coefficient of $x^2$ in the polynomial
$$(1-x)^2(1+2x)^2(1-3x)^2\cdots(1-11x)^2.$$
(The factors alternate in sign: the $k$th factor is $(1+(-1)^k kx)^2$.)

bmt-2016-analysis-09.prompt:
Suppose $p''(x)=4x^2+4x+2$ where
$$p(x)=a_0+a_1(x-1)+a_2(x-2)^2+a_3(x-3)^3+a_4(x-4)^4.$$
We have $p'(-3)=-24$ and $p(x)$ has the unique property that the sum of the third powers of the roots of $p(x)$ is equal to the sum of the fourth powers of the roots of $p(x)$. Find $a_0$.
bmt-2016-analysis-09.reviewNote: The printed paper has the term a_3(x-3)^4 (apparently a typo for (x-3)^3); with the printed exponent a_0 would be 77/2, so the intended (x-3)^3 is used, which matches the official answer -2.
